why: A class cannot be its own superclass, however far up: MATLAB refuses a circular class definition, so no method is inherited along such a chain. `obj.wilt()` in `Thorn < Briar` calls the inherited `Briar::wilt`; once `Briar.m` says `Briar < Thorn` the chain comes back to `Thorn`, and the call links nowhere; with `Briar < handle` back it links again. A class's own method is still linked (project rule: the sync follows a chain upwards only; see methodOnHierarchy in matlab-lookup.ts). Each step must end where a fresh index ends (project rule; the shape of the step 15 fuzz find s2005-c6).

edit.Briar.m:
classdef Briar < Thorn
  methods
    function r = wilt(obj)
      r = 1;
    end
  end
end

classdef Briar < handle
  methods
    function r = wilt(obj)
      r = 1;
    end
  end
end
